instruction: Design a single-page introduction screen for a colorful side-scrolling platform adventure inspired by classic mascot platformers. Include a bold original game title, a hero beside a layered level preview with platforms, blocks, coins, enemies, and a distant goal, plus a prominent Start Adventure button, small controls guide, world selector, and collectible counters. Put strong emphasis on a joyful original identity, clear gameplay storytelling, depth, expressive shapes, and a polished launch-screen composition.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: All required elements exist, but two are under-delivered. 'A hero beside a layered level preview' becomes a tiny hero inside the preview, so the mascot is never the focal character; the 'small controls guide' is reduced to a one-line 'press Enter' hint with no movement/jump keys. The world selector is pushed below the fold (cards clipped at the bottom edge), so the 'single-page launch screen' actually requires scrolling. Clarity & Hierarchy: The title wraps mid-word as 'SKYBOU / NCE', reading as a layout bug rather than a bold lockup, and it duplicates the top-left 'SKYBOUNCE' wordmark at a second scale. The white 'Save synced' pill and sound chip read as SaaS app chrome, breaking the game fantasy and adding non-brief elements to the top bar. The helper text beside the CTA is low-contrast, and the 'CHAPTER ONE' pill plus 'World 1-1' chip redundantly state the same selection. Visual System & Craft: The mid-word title break, the indented second line, and the red→yellow gradient spanning the broken word look unfinished. The preview is flat against a brief that stresses 'layered' and 'depth': one ground band, one hill silhouette, no parallax separation, plain-circle sun. The logo mark (red square with a dot) doesn't match the red blob mascot. Counter-card accents don't consistently map to in-game items, and the CTA's hard offset shadow is the only game-feel shadow in an otherwise soft-SaaS shadow language. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The composition is a generic two-column hero of pills and cards; the mascot is the smallest character on screen; nothing moves (static coins, flag, enemies), so the 'joyful, bouncy' identity is asserted in copy but not shown. Real trade-offs: (1) title scale vs. column width — the current width forces the ugly wrap; an intentional stacked lockup or wider span keeps boldness without the break. (2) single-viewport launch vs. including the world selector — the left column is too tall; compressing copy/counters and converting the world grid to a compact horizontal chip row keeps all required content on one screen. (3) hero inside vs. beside the preview — pulling the mascot out and overlapping the card edge satisfies the brief and creates a focal moment, at the cost of a busier card border. (4) utility vs. diegetic chrome — the sound toggle is useful but should be restyled in-world; 'Save synced' can survive as a small diegetic badge rather than a white app pill.
history.suggestion: One prioritized plan (fully offline, no external assets): 1) Rebuild the title as an intentional lockup: either a single line sized with clamp() to fit the column, or a deliberate two-line 'SKY / BOUNCE' stack with equal letter sizes, aligned baselines, and the star/cloud integrated into the letters; reduce the top-left wordmark to just the mascot mark to kill the duplicate. 2) Rebalance to a true 100vh launch screen: cut body copy to two lines, keep the three counters as one compact row, and move 'Choose Your World' up as a horizontal strip of 3–4 chunky world chips (locked/unlocked states, current world highlighted) so nothing scrolls. 3) Feature the mascot: enlarge the hero ~3x and place it overlapping the bottom-left edge of the level preview card (beside it) with a CSS idle-bounce animation; remove the tiny duplicate hero from inside the scene. 4) Add depth to the preview: three parallax layers (drifting far cloud band, mid hills, near grass tufts), spinning coins, bobbing enemies, a waving flag, and an inner shadow/vignette on the card. 5) Add a real controls guide: a row of chunky keycaps (← → move · Space jump · Enter start) beside the CTA, using the same border/shadow tokens as the cards. 6) Make Start Adventure the dominant control: larger, with a pulsing glow on hover/press and a higher-contrast Enter hint. 7) Restyle chrome diegetically: replace the white 'Save synced' pill with a small cloud badge ('Progress saved'), restyle the sound toggle as a chunky in-world button, and swap the logo mark for the mascot's face. 8) Unify the craft system: one radius scale, one shadow token (soft ambient + hard offset reserved for interactive game elements), counter bars colored to match their in-game item (coin yellow, bubble teal, star red), and a 4-color palette with defined tints applied consistently.
